title: urn:qauth:ia:identifier:v1-rc.0
description: Identifier-first sign-in (ADR-020 §3). Every identifier, known or unknown, gets the same next step, so the screen reveals nothing about which accounts exist (ADR-017 Decision 4). Offered as an alternative of a later step, it is the account switch: answering it ends the interaction and starts a new one for the same authorization request, and the result is a redirect to the ceremony app’s page of the new interaction. Nothing proved for the first account carries over (#592). Beside `select_account` it is "Use another account", which ends no session: it adds an account, and the accounts the chooser lists stay signed in (ADR-019 Decision 3). Beside any other step it is "Not you?", which also signs the browser out of the account the screen shows, and of no other account, so that the next person or the next app on a shared device does not continue as that account; its label says that it signs out (#964). The account shown is the one a sign-in during the interaction proved, the signed-in user a consent is for or, while nobody has signed in during the interaction, the account the identifier the person gave names. Its sessions that end: the one a sign-in during the interaction started (#896); the session the browser was already signed in with when the interaction started, such as for a consent or a sign-in the app asked for again, when it is that account’s (#964); and, when the server can check the browser’s session cookie, the session it names if that belongs to the same account (a sign-in again in another tab). The cookie is cleared when it names one of them. A session of another account stays.

login_hint.description: The identifier: today an email address of at most 254 bytes in UTF-8 (ADR-017 Decision 3). The schema counts characters; the server counts bytes, checks the full email syntax and normalises the address before use.

personal.description: What the screen pre-fills the identifier field with.

login_hint.description: The authorization request's `login_hint` (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.2.1), for the screen to pre-fill the identifier field with (#628). The client chose it, so it is only a suggestion: the person answers the step with it or with another identifier, and the server checks that answer as it checks any other. Absent when the request carried none or one that is no display value, and after an account switch.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 `amr` values a successful answer adds to the transaction: none, because the step proves no authenticator.
